facts.raw_span: progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over the preceding 5 days
no prior medical history
alert (GCS 15), afebrile, and appeared well
both external ear canals were obstructed by effusion and cerumen
routine blood tests were unremarkable
Three-month history of “ear problems”
initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation
bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal
adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated a threshold of 40 dB with normal wave latencies on the left
80 dB threshold with prolonged wave I latency on the right, indicating profound right-sided hearing loss
no nystagmus

concepts.why: The patient has a history of ear problems, including otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation, and current examination shows bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and external auditory canal, consistent with cholesteatoma.

The patient presents with progressive unsteadiness, recurrent falls, and hearing loss, which are consistent with labyrinthitis, an inner ear inflammation that can cause vestibular and auditory symptoms.
The patient has a history of otitis media with effusion, which is consistent with the current examination findings of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and external auditory canal.
The patient has a history of ear problems and current examination shows bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, consistent with mastoiditis, an infection of the mastoid bone.
The patient has adenoid hypertrophy, which is consistent with the current examination findings and can contribute to ear problems and hearing loss.

rationales.F01: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls suggest a vestibular or balance issue, which could be related to Cholesteatoma or Labyrinthitis.
rationales.F04: Obstruction of the external ear canals by effusion and cerumen could be related to Cholesteatoma or Otitis media with effusion.
rationales.F06: A history of ear problems could be related to Cholesteatoma, Otitis media with effusion, or Mastoiditis.
rationales.F07: Initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation could be related to Cholesteatoma or Otitis media with effusion.
rationales.F08: Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal is highly suggestive of Cholesteatoma or Mastoiditis.
rationales.F11: Profound right-sided hearing loss could be related to Cholesteatoma or Labyrinthitis.
rationales.F12: Absence of nystagmus makes Labyrinthitis less likely.
